props.gloss_en: all sacred writings are rescued from a fire, whether they are read or not, even if written in any language
they require burial
Rav Huna: sacred writings written in translation or in any language are not rescued from a fire
Rav Chisda: they are rescued from a fire
on the view that they were given to be read, all agree they are rescued; they argue on the view that they were not given to be read
Rav Huna: not rescued, since they were not given to be read
Rav Chisda: rescued, because of the disgrace to sacred writings
Rav Huna's reading: 'read' is the Prophets, 'not read' the Writings; that is when written in the holy tongue, but in any other language they are not rescued -- and even so they require burial
Rav Chisda's reading: even written in any language they are rescued; and the seifa means: their worm-eaten remnants require burial
the baraita: written in translation or any language -- they are rescued from a fire
Rav Huna: this tanna holds they were given to be read
the baraita: written in Coptic, Median, Ivrit, Elamite or Greek, though not given to be read -- they are rescued from a fire
Rav Huna: it is a tannaitic dispute
the tanna kama: written in translation or any language -- they are rescued
R' Yosei: they are not rescued from a fire
Yochanan HaNazuf: I remember Rabban Gamliel your grandfather on a step of the Temple Mount; they brought him a Job targum and he told the builder: sink it under the course of stones
he too [Rabban Gamliel b'Rabbi, found reading a Job targum] ordered it and buried it
R' Yosei b'R' Yehuda: they overturned a tub of mortar on it
Rebbi: is it permitted to destroy them by hand?
Rebbi: rather, one leaves them in a neglected place and they rot of themselves
[proposed:] Rav Huna's tannaim are the tanna kama and R' Yosei
rather, Rav Huna's tannaim are R' Yosei and the tanna of the Coptic baraita
the baraita: blessings and amulets, though they contain letters of the Name and many Torah matters, are not rescued from a fire but burn in their place, they and their Names
from here they said: writers of blessings are like burners of Torah
R' Yishmael [to the writer who sank the bundle of blessings in water]: the punishment for the latter is greater than for the former
sacred writings in the holy tongue but written in arsenic, red paint, gum or vitriol are rescued from a fire
Rabba bar Rav Huna: they are not rescued
[the stam, on the view 'not rescued':] perhaps that is only for translation and any language, but here, in the holy tongue, they are rescued
[the stam, on the view 'rescued':] perhaps that is only for writing in durable ink, but here, since it does not last, not
the baraita: the only difference between books and the megilla is that books are written in any language, while the megilla must be in Assyrian script, on parchment, and in ink
Rav Huna bar Chaluv: where [the portion] lacks letters of 'vayehi binsoa' I do not ask: since it contains the Names, though it lacks 85 letters, it is rescued
Rav Nachman: a Torah scroll without enough to collect 85 letters is not rescued

the baraita: translation written as scripture, scripture written as translation, and Ivrit script are rescued, and needless to say the Aramaic in Ezra, in Daniel and in the Torah [= 'Yegar Sahaduta', which has fewer than 85 letters]
Rav Huna: the 85 letters must be contiguous
Rav Chisda: even scattered
the baraita: a worn Torah scroll, if it has enough to collect 85 letters, like 'vayehi binsoa', is rescued; if not, not
the baraita: the Holy One made signs above and below this portion, to say that this is not its place
Rebbi: not for that reason, but because it is an important book by itself
R' Yonatan: 'she carved her seven pillars' (Prov 9:1) -- these are the seven books of the Torah
whose view is R' Yonatan's? Rebbi's
the tanna who disputes Rebbi is Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
RSBG: this portion will in the future be uprooted from here and written in its place
RSBG: it was written here to separate between the first punishment and the second
the second punishment is 'and the people were as complainers' (Num 11:1)
the first punishment is 'and they travelled from the mountain of the Lord' (Num 10:33)
R' Chama b'R' Chanina: [it means] that they turned away from after the Lord
Rav Ashi: its place is in [the portion of] the banners
[candidate answer:] the blank margins of a Torah scroll are not rescued from a fire
[candidate answer:] the blank margins of a Torah scroll are rescued from a fire
the baraita: an erased Torah scroll, if it has enough to collect 85 letters, is rescued; if not, not
the margins above and below, between portions, between columns, at the start and end of the scroll, render the hands impure
the baraita: blank folios and the books of heretics are not rescued from a fire, but burn in their place, they and their Names
R' Yosei: on a weekday one cuts out the Names in them and buries them, and burns the rest
R' Tarfon (an oath on his sons): if they come into my hands I will burn them together with the Names in them
R' Tarfon: even if a man pursues him to kill him and a snake runs to bite him, one enters a house of idolatry and not the houses of these
R' Tarfon: for these know and deny, and those do not know and deny
R' Tarfon: of them the verse says 'behind the door and the doorpost you have set your remembrance' (Isa 57:8)
R' Yishmael: of them David said 'do I not hate those who hate You, Lord... I hate them with utmost hatred, they have become my enemies' (Ps 139:21-22)
and just as they are not rescued from a fire, so they are not rescued from a collapse, from water, or from anything that destroys them
Rav would not go to the house of Avidan, all the more so to the house of Nitzrefei
Shmuel would not go to the house of Nitzrefei, but would go to the house of Avidan
Rava [asked why he did not come to the house of Avidan]: there is a certain palm tree on the way, and it is hard for me
[they:] we will uproot it
Rava: its place [the pit] is hard for me
Mar bar Yosef: I am one of them, and I do not fear them
once he went, and they sought to endanger him
R' Meir would call it 'aven gilyon' (the folio of iniquity)
R' Yochanan would call it 'avon gilyon' (the folio of sin)
there was a philosopher in their neighbourhood who had a name for not taking bribes; they wanted to expose him
she brought him a golden lamp, and they came before him
Imma Shalom: I want them to give me a share of my father's-house estate
the philosopher: divide
it is written for us: where there is a son, a daughter does not inherit
the philosopher: since the day you were exiled from your land the Torah of Moses was taken away and the avon gilyon was given
the philosopher: and in it is written, son and daughter shall inherit alike
the next day he [Rabban Gamliel] in turn brought him a Libyan donkey
the philosopher: I went down to the end of the avon gilyon, and in it is written: I came not to subtract from the Torah of Moses nor to add to the Torah of Moses
Imma Shalom: let your light shine like a lamp
Rabban Gamliel: the donkey came and kicked over the lamp

supports.gloss_en: דתניא: היו כתובין תרגום ובכל לשון -- מצילין; רבי יוסי אומר: אין מצילין
אמר רבי יוסי: מעשה באבא חלפתא ... ובידו ספר איוב תרגום והוא קורא בו ... אף הוא צוה עליו וגנזו -- a Job targum was buried rather than read
מאי תניא? אמר רב אשי, כדתניא: אין בין ספרים למגילה ... ומגילה ... ובדיו -- only the megilla needs ink, so books written otherwise are still sacred
seven books only if 'vayehi binsoa' is a book by itself, as Rebbi says
דתניא: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר: עתידה פרשה זו שתיעקר מכאן ותכתב במקומה
תא שמע: ספר תורה שבלה ... ואם לאו אין מצילין. ואמאי, תיפוק ליה משום גיליון דידיה! -- so margins are not rescued

deflected_by.gloss_en: בלה שאני -- a worn scroll is different

supports.gloss_en: תא שמע: ספר תורה שנמחק ... ואם לאו אין מצילין. ואמאי? תיפוק ליה משום גיליון דידיה!

deflected_by.gloss_en: מקום הכתב לא קמיבעיא לי, דכי קדוש אגב כתב הוא דקדוש, אזל כתב אזלא לה קדושתיה. כי קמיבעיא לי של מעלה ושל מטה, שבין פרשה לפרשה, שבין דף לדף, שבתחלת הספר, שבסוף הספר

refuted_by.gloss_en: ותיפוק ליה משום ההוא! -- then let it be rescued on account of those [margins]

deflected_by.gloss_en: דגיז ושדי -- [the margins] were cut off and thrown away

supports.gloss_en: תא שמע: הגליונין ... מטמאין את הידים! -- so they are sacred

deflected_by.gloss_en: דילמא אגב ספר תורה שאני -- perhaps as part of the scroll it is different

supports.gloss_en: תא שמע: הגליונין וספרי מינין אין מצילין ... מאי לאו, גליונין דספר תורה?

deflected_by.gloss_en: לא, גליונין דספרי מינין. [attacked:] השתא ספרי מינין גופייהו אין מצילין, גליונין מבעיא? [defended:] הכי קאמר: וספרי מינין הרי הן כגליונים

supports.gloss_en: ועליהן הכתוב אומר: אחר הדלת והמזוזה שמת זכרונך

frames.gloss_en: מאן תנאי? -- which tannaim are Rav Huna's 'tannaitic dispute'?

alternatives.gloss_en: אילימא תנא קמא דרבי יוסי -- eliminated

eliminated_by.gloss_en: ודילמא בהא קמיפלגי: מר סבר ניתנו לקרות בהן, ומר סבר לא ניתנו לקרות בהן -- their dispute may be over whether they were given to be read, which does not touch Rav Huna's

alternatives.gloss_en: the survivor: אלא רבי יוסי ותנא דגיפטית

objections.gloss_en: תנן: כל כתבי הקדש מצילין... מאי לאו, 'שקורין בהן' -- נביאים, 'ושאין קורין בהן' -- כתובים, 'אף על פי שכתובין בכל לשון' -- דלא ניתנו לקרות בהן, וקתני מצילין -- ותיובתא דרב הונא!

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר לך רב הונא: ותסברא? אימא סיפא: טעונין גניזה -- השתא אצולי מצילינן, גניזה מיבעיא? -- the objector's reading makes the seifa redundant; rather the mishnah speaks of the holy tongue (= p_huna_reading)

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: היו כתובים תרגום וכל לשון -- מצילין אותן מפני הדליקה. תיובתא דרב הונא!

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר לך רב הונא: האי תנא סבר ניתנו לקרות בהן (= p_huna_tanna_nitnu)

objections.gloss_en: תא שמע: היו כתובין גיפטית... אף על פי שלא ניתנו לקרות בהן -- מצילין. תיובתא דרב הונא!

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר לך רב הונא: תנאי היא (= p_huna_tannaei), דתניא ... רבי יוסי אומר: אין מצילין

objections.gloss_en: שתי תשובות בדבר: חדא, וכי טיט בהר הבית מנין? -- where would mortar come from on the Temple Mount?
ועוד, וכי מותר לאבדן ביד? -- and is it permitted to destroy them by hand?
והא רב המנונא תנא מצילין! -- answered only by אי תניא תניא, i.e. deference (encoded as Rabba bar Rav Huna's retract)
איתיביה: ... ואין צריך לומר תרגום שבעזרא ושבדניאל ושבתורה -- תרגום שבתורה מאי ניהו? יגר שהדותא, ואף על גב דלית בה שמונים וחמש אותיות!

answered_by.gloss_en: כי תניא ההיא -- להשלים: that baraita speaks of it completing the 85 (unmarked, so the stam's; Steinsaltz gives it to Rav Nachman)

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: ספר תורה שבלה, אם יש בו ללקט שמונים וחמש אותיות... מצילין -- 'to collect' implies scattered. תיובתא דרב הונא!

answered_by.gloss_en: תרגמה רב חסדא אליבא דרב הונא: בתיבות -- scattered letters, but within whole words
